functions.name: oz.RateAtDateλ
functions.summary: Returns the rate in effect on each date from a table of effective dates and rates, refusing gaps, unsorted or repeated dates

parameters.text: The rate that applies from each effective date, the same length as EffectiveDates.

functions.name: oz.LeaseLiabilityλ
functions.summary: Present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date
functions.description: Present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date.

parameters.name: Payments
parameters.text: One row or one column of lease payments, one per period, entered positive. Include the measurement-date payment first when InAdvance is TRUE.

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.text: Discount rate per period, not per year.

parameters.name: InAdvance
parameters.text: TRUE when the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date.

notes: AASB 16 paragraph 26 measures the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments not paid at the commencement date, discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease where that rate can be readily determined and at the lessee's incremental borrowing rate where it cannot. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date and excluded from the liability. Add a payment made at or before commencement to the right-of-use asset cost instead. Rate is per period. Convert an effective annual rate with PeriodRateλ(AnnualRate, PeriodsPerYear). Divide a nominal annual rate by PeriodsPerYear only when its compounding periods match the payments. Include an amount expected to be payable under a residual value guarantee, or the exercise price of a purchase option, in the final period where paragraph 27 brings it into the lease payments. IRRλ() over the same cash flows gives an implicit rate per year; convert it to the rate per period, (1 + annual) ^ (1 / 12) - 1 for months, before passing it here. Arithmetic only: this does not determine the lease term, decide what is a lease payment, or decide whether the arrangement contains a lease. AASB 16 compilation checked 24 August 2026.

functions.name: oz.LeaseScheduleλ
functions.summary: Unwinds an AASB 16 lease liability: opening, payment, interest and closing for each period
functions.description: Unwinds an AASB 16 lease liability over its term.

parameters.name: Payments
parameters.text: One row or one column of lease payments, one per period, entered positive. Include the measurement-date payment first when InAdvance is TRUE.

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.text: Discount rate per period, not per year.

parameters.name: InAdvance
parameters.text: TRUE when the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date.

notes: Returns four rows: opening liability, payment, interest, closing liability. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date and is excluded from both the opening liability and the payment row. Each remaining payment follows one period of interest, so closing is opening plus interest less payment and the last closing balance is nil. The result has one fewer column for payments in advance; a sole measurement-date payment returns one zero column. The opening balance is LeaseLiabilityλ() on the same arguments. Pair this with ROUScheduleλ() for the asset that sits opposite it: the two together give the front-loaded expense profile AASB 16 produces. Arithmetic only, on the payments and rate you supply.

functions.name: oz.LeaseRemeasureλ
functions.summary: Remeasures an AASB 16 lease liability for revised payments and adjusts the right-of-use asset
functions.description: Remeasures a lease liability for revised payments and adjusts the asset.

parameters.name: RevisedPayments
parameters.text: Revised lease payments for the remaining term, one per period, positive. Include a payment made at the remeasurement date first when InAdvance is TRUE.

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.text: Discount rate per period. Unchanged, unless a floating rate moved.

parameters.name: CarryingLiability
parameters.text: Lease liability before remeasurement and before any payment due that day. Do not deduct the first revised payment.

parameters.name: CarryingROU
parameters.text: Right-of-use asset carried immediately before the remeasurement.

parameters.name: InAdvance
parameters.text: TRUE when the first revised payment is paid at the remeasurement date.

notes: Returns four rows: revised lease liability, adjustment, revised right-of-use asset, amount recognised in profit or loss. AASB 16 paragraph 42(b) remeasures the liability where future payments change because an index or a rate used to determine them has changed, and only when the cash flows change. Paragraph 43 keeps the discount rate unchanged for that revision, and uses a revised rate only where the change arises from a floating interest rate, so pass the original rate unless it is the rate itself that moved. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first revised payment is paid at the remeasurement date and excluded from the revised liability. Paragraph 39 takes the remeasurement to the right-of-use asset, and where that asset is reduced to nil any further reduction goes to profit or loss: row four carries that remainder, negative, because it is a credit. Arithmetic only. AASB 16 compilation checked 24 August 2026.

functions.name: oz.ROUScheduleλ
functions.summary: Straight-line right-of-use asset schedule: opening, depreciation and closing for each period
functions.description: Depreciates a right-of-use asset in a straight line over the lease term.

parameters.name: Cost
parameters.text: Initial carrying amount of the right-of-use asset.

parameters.name: Periods
parameters.text: Number of periods to depreciate over, at least 1.

notes: Returns three rows: opening carrying amount, depreciation, closing carrying amount. AASB 16 paragraph 24 measures the asset at cost, comprising the initial lease liability, lease payments made at or before the commencement date less incentives received, initial direct costs, and an estimate of dismantling and restoration costs. Add those up yourself and pass the total as Cost. Depreciate over the lease term where ownership does not transfer, and over the useful life where it does. Cost and Periods are single values, not arrays. Arithmetic only. AASB 16 compilation checked 24 August 2026.

functions.name: oz.PeriodRateλ
functions.summary: Converts an effective annual rate to the equivalent rate per period, the rate the lease functions take
functions.description: Converts an effective annual rate to the equivalent rate per period.

parameters.name: AnnualRate
parameters.text: Effective annual rate, or a row or column of them.

parameters.name: PeriodsPerYear
parameters.text: Periods in a year: 12 for months, 4 for quarters, 1 for years.

notes: (1 + AnnualRate) ^ (1 / PeriodsPerYear) - 1, so compounding the result PeriodsPerYear times gives the annual rate back. This is the rate per period that LeaseLiabilityλ(), LeaseScheduleλ() and LeaseRemeasureλ() take. It is for an effective annual rate. A nominal annual percentage rate that compounds monthly is already APR / 12 per month, so do not pass it here; EFFECT() turns one into the effective rate this takes. AnnualRateλ() is the inverse.

functions.name: oz.DayCountRateλ
functions.summary: Interest rate for each period of a timeline under a day count convention: 30/360, Actual/360, Actual/365 or Actual/Actual
functions.description: Interest rate for each period of a timeline under a day count convention.

parameters.name: Timeline
parameters.text: A row or column of period dates, at least two, evenly spaced.

parameters.name: APR
parameters.text: Annual percentage rate, one value or one per period.

parameters.name: Convention
parameters.text: 1 = 30/360, 2 = Actual/360, 3 = Actual/365, 4 = Actual/Actual. Any other number is #VALUE!.

parameters.name: EndDates
parameters.text: TRUE, or a number other than 0, when the timeline shows period end dates rather than start dates.

notes: Returns a row with one rate per timeline period, whichever way the timeline runs: APR multiplied by the days in the period and divided by the days in the year, as the convention counts them. Pass the result to DebtSculptVariableλ() or DebtSculptVariableLRVλ() as PeriodRates in place of a flat twelfth of the APR. With start dates each period runs from its date to the day before the next, and the last period takes its length from the one before it; with end dates each runs from the day after the previous date to its own, and the first period is the one inferred. A gap of 28 days or more is read as whole calendar months, a shorter one as days. 30/360 counts every month as 30 days on the European rule. Under Actual/Actual each calendar year uses its own length as the denominator (the ISDA rule), including periods spanning several years.

functions.name: oz.ATOTurnoverλ
functions.summary: Turnover as the ATO small business benchmarks measure it: other sales unless under half of total business income
functions.description: Turnover excluding GST, the denominator of every ATO tax return benchmark ratio.

parameters.name: OtherSales
parameters.text: Other sales of goods and services, excluding GST.

parameters.name: TotalBusinessIncome
parameters.text: Total business income, excluding GST.

notes: Returns OtherSales, unless it is zero, blank or less than half of TotalBusinessIncome, when it returns TotalBusinessIncome instead. That is the ATO's rule. OtherSales is the other sales of goods and services amount on the return. Where total business income is blank or incomplete, the ATO adds up the business income items it lists for the return type: pass that total as TotalBusinessIncome. Pass both amounts excluding GST. functions.name: oz.ATOBenchmarkRatioλ
functions.summary: ATO tax return benchmark ratio: an amount divided by turnover, as for rent or motor vehicle expenses to turnover
functions.description: ATO tax return benchmark ratio: Amount / Turnover.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.text: The expense amount, excluding GST.

parameters.name: Turnover
parameters.text: Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

notes: The ATO's basic formula for a tax return benchmark ratio, and the whole of its rent expenses to turnover and motor vehicle expenses to turnover ratios: pass the rent or motor vehicle expenses amount from the return. Returns a fraction; format it as a percentage, as the ATO's figure is the same quotient multiplied by 100. Take Turnover from ATOTurnoverλ(). Use ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ(), ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ() and ATOLabourRatioλ() for the 3 ratios whose amounts the ATO adjusts. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

functions.name: oz.ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ
functions.summary: ATO total expenses to turnover: total expenses less payments to associated persons, over turnover
functions.description: ATO total expenses to turnover benchmark ratio.

parameters.name: TotalExpenses
parameters.text: Total expenses from the return, excluding GST.

parameters.name: Turnover
parameters.text: Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

parameters.name: AssociatePayments
parameters.text: Payments to associated persons.

notes: (TotalExpenses - AssociatePayments) / Turnover. The ATO deducts payments to associated persons from total expenses before dividing. Where total expenses is blank or incomplete, it adds up the expense items it lists for the return type: pass that total as TotalExpenses. OperatingRatioλ() gives the same quotient only when its expenses already exclude those payments and its net sales equal this Turnover. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank AssociatePayments counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

functions.name: oz.ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ
functions.summary: ATO cost of sales to turnover, excluding salary and wages included in cost of sales
functions.description: ATO cost of sales to turnover benchmark ratio, excluding labour.

parameters.name: CostOfSales
parameters.text: Cost of sales from the return, excluding GST.

parameters.name: Turnover
parameters.text: Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

parameters.name: IncludedWages
parameters.text: Total salary and wages expenses, only when the return's code is C.

notes: (CostOfSales - IncludedWages) / Turnover. The ATO's cost of sales excludes salary and wages: where the return's total salary and wages code is C, meaning they are included in cost of sales, it deducts the total salary and wages expenses. Pass that total as IncludedWages only when the code is C, and leave it out otherwise. GrossMarginλ() is a different measure: it keeps wages in cost of sales. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank IncludedWages counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

functions.name: oz.ATOLabourRatioλ
functions.summary: ATO labour to turnover: salary and wages plus contractors less payments to associated persons, over turnover
functions.description: ATO labour to turnover benchmark ratio.

parameters.name: SalaryWages
parameters.text: Total salary and wages expenses from the return.

parameters.name: Contractors
parameters.text: Contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses.

parameters.name: Turnover
parameters.text: Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

parameters.name: AssociatePayments
parameters.text: Payments to associated persons.

parameters.name: W1
parameters.text: The year's total at activity statement label W1.

notes: (Wages + Contractors - AssociatePayments) / Turnover, where Wages is SalaryWages, or W1 when W1 is greater. The ATO adds total salary and wages expenses to contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses and deducts payments to associated persons. Where the activity statements' label W1 (total salary, wages and other payments) for the year exceeds the return's salary and wages, it uses W1. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank AssociatePayments or W1 counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

functions.name: oz.ReceivableDaysλ
functions.summary: Receivable days, or days sales outstanding (DSO): Receivables / Sales x Days
functions.description: Receivable days, or days sales outstanding (DSO): the days of sales not yet collected.

parameters.name: Receivables
parameters.text: Trade receivables: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

parameters.name: Sales
parameters.text: Credit sales over the same Days.

parameters.name: Days
parameters.text: Days the Sales figure covers.

notes: Receivables / Sales * Days. Days is the number of days the Sales figure covers: 365 with a year's sales, 90 with the last three months' sales for a rolling figure, or a month's days with that month's sales. Pass closing receivables, or the average of opening and closing for an average-balance figure. Put the balance and the sales on the same basis: where one includes GST and the other does not, adjust the inputs first, because this function makes no GST adjustment. Sales of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

functions.name: oz.PayableDaysλ
functions.summary: Payable days, or days payable outstanding (DPO): Payables / Purchases x Days
functions.description: Payable days, or days payable outstanding (DPO): the days of purchases not yet paid.

parameters.name: Payables
parameters.text: Trade payables: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

parameters.name: Purchases
parameters.text: Credit purchases, or cost of sales, over the same Days.

parameters.name: Days
parameters.text: Days the Purchases figure covers.

notes: Payables / Purchases * Days. Days is the number of days the Purchases figure covers, as for ReceivableDaysλ(). Credit purchases are the matching flow; cost of sales is the common substitute where purchases are not reported. Pass closing payables, or the average of opening and closing. Put the balance and the purchases on the same basis: where one includes GST and the other does not, adjust the inputs first, because this function makes no GST adjustment. Purchases of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

functions.name: oz.WIPDaysλ
functions.summary: Work in progress days: WIP / RelatedFlow x Days, with both on one valuation basis
functions.description: Work in progress days: the days of work done but not yet billed or completed.

parameters.name: WIP
parameters.text: Work in progress: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

parameters.name: RelatedFlow
parameters.text: Fee revenue or cost of sales over the same Days, on the valuation basis of WIP.

parameters.name: Days
parameters.text: Days the RelatedFlow figure covers.

notes: WIP / RelatedFlow * Days. WIP and RelatedFlow must use the same valuation basis: fee revenue with WIP at charge-out value, as a professional services firm records it, or cost of sales with WIP at cost. Days is the number of days the RelatedFlow figure covers. WIP days plus ReceivableDaysλ() gives the lock-up days a services firm tracks. RelatedFlow of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

functions.name: oz.CashConversionCycleλ
functions.summary: Cash conversion cycle in days: inventory days + WIP days + receivable days - payable days
functions.description: Cash conversion cycle: the days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

parameters.name: InventoryDays
parameters.text: Inventory days, for example from DSIλ().

parameters.name: ReceivableDays
parameters.text: Receivable days, for example from ReceivableDaysλ().

parameters.name: PayableDays
parameters.text: Payable days, for example from PayableDaysλ().

parameters.name: WIPDays
parameters.text: Work in progress days, for example from WIPDaysλ().

notes: InventoryDays + WIPDays + ReceivableDays - PayableDays. Pass day counts, for example from DSIλ(), ReceivableDaysλ(), PayableDaysλ() and WIPDaysλ(), with every component on the same period basis. DSIλ() multiplies by 365 and expects a full year's cost of goods sold, so for a shorter window annualise that window's cost of goods sold before passing it. A negative result means suppliers are paid after customers pay. An omitted or blank WIPDays counts as 0. Pass WIPDays only where WIP is not already in the inventory behind InventoryDays, or it is counted twice.
